text:
GRU4Rec’s BPR-max addresses gradient dilution from averaging many easy pairwise negatives. With negative scores r_j, weights w=softmax(r_neg), its regularized objective is −log Σ_j w_j·sigmoid(r_pos−r_j) + λΣ_j w_j·r_j². The logarithm encloses the weighted probability sum; averaging weighted log-sigmoids implements a different loss. High-scoring negatives receive more emphasis without discrete hardest-item selection. [Original paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf). The official implementation recommends cross-entropy or BPR-max and supports sampling-distribution logQ correction for cross-entropy. [GRU4Rec repository](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).

Sampled softmax provides an alternative with implicit hard-negative emphasis; research identifies ranking and popularity-bias benefits, while warning that cosine-normalized representations can limit magnitude learning. These findings motivate comparison, but establish no winner for this Amazon benchmark. [Sampled-softmax study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.02327). False negatives remain a concern: unobserved items can reflect latent interest. UFNRec studies exploiting such samples, although its teacher-based method is unnecessary for the proposed single-model experiment. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116).

Suggested ablation: retain one GRU4Rec model per category; compare regularized BPR-max against sampled softmax using matched negative pools. Then test conservative hard sampling from a larger random pool, retaining random negatives and excluding padding, current positives and observed training-history positives. Treat hardness as informativeness, not proof of irrelevance; temperature smoothing or semi-hard selection are hypotheses for reducing false-negative damage. Never use held-out interactions to filter training negatives. Keep seeds and training limits fixed, selecting exclusively by macro validation HR@10 across all four categories; Electronics separation alone cannot establish improvement.
